source_text: Τούτων ἤδη προδιηνυσμένων ἑπόμενον ἂν εἴη τὸν παιδαγωγὸν ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν τὸν βίον ἡμῖν τὸν ἀληθινὸν ὑποτυπώσασθαι καὶ τὸν ἐν Χριστῷ παιδαγωγῆσαι ἄνθρωπον. ἔστι δὲ ὁ χαρακτηρισμὸς οὐ φοβερὸς ἄγαν αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ ἔκλυτος κομιδῇ ὑπὸ χρηστότητος. ἐντέλλεται δὲ ἅμα καὶ χαρακτηρίζει τὰς ἐντολὰς ὡς ἡμᾶς αὐτὰς ἐκτελεῖν δύνασθαι. καί μοι δοκεῖ αὐτὸς οὗτος πλάσαι μὲν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ χοός, ἀναγεννῆσαι δὲ ὕδατι, αὐξῆσαι δὲ πνεύματι, παιδαγωγῆσαι δὲ ῥήματι, εἰς υἱοθεσίαν καὶ σωτηρίαν ἁγίαις ἐντολαῖς κατευθύνων, ἵνα δὴ τὸν γηγενῆ εἰς ἅγιον καὶ ἐπουράνιον μεταπλάσας ἐκ προσβάσεως ἄνθρωπον, ἐκείνην τὴν θεϊκὴν μάλιστα πληρώσῃ φωνήν· »ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ᾿ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ᾿ ὁμοίωσιν ἡμῶν.« καὶ δὴ γέγονεν ὁ Χριστὸς τοῦτο πλῆρες, ὅπερ εἴρηκεν ὁ θεός, ὁ δὲ ἄλλος ἄνθρωπος κατὰ μόνην νοεῖται τὴν εἰκόνα. ἡμεῖς δέ, ὦ παῖδες ἀγαθοῦ πατρός, ἀγαθοῦ παιδαγωγοῦ θρέμματα, πληρώσωμεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός, ἀκούωμεν τοῦ λόγου καὶ τὸν σωτήριον ὄντως ἀναμαξώμεθα τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν βίον· ἐνθένδε ἤδη τὴν ἐπουράνιον μελετῶντες πολιτείαν, καθ᾿ ἣν ἐκθεούμεθα, τὸ ἀειθαλὲς εὐφροσύνης καὶ ἀκήρατον εὐωδίας ἐπαλειφώμεθα χρῖσμα, ἐναργὲς ὑπόδειγμα ἀφθαρσίας τὴν πολιτείαν ἔχοντες τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τὰ ἴχνη τοῦ θεοῦ διώκοντες· ᾧ μόνῳ προσήκει σκοπεῖν καὶ δὴ μέλει πῶς καὶ τίνα τρόπον ὑγιεινότερος ἂν ὁ τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίος γένοιτο. ἀλλὰ καὶ πρὸς αὐτάρκειαν τοῦ βίου καὶ ἀπεριττότητα ἔτι τε εὔζωνόν τε καὶ εὔλυτον ὁδοιπορικὴν ἑτοιμότητα εἰς ἀιδιότητα εὐζωΐας παρασκευάζει, αὐτὸν αὑτοῦ ἕκαστον ἡμῶν ταμιεῖον εἶναι διδάσκων. »μὴ γὰρ μεριμνᾶτε«, φησί, »περὶ τῆς αὔριον«, χρῆναι λέγων τὸν ἀπογεγραμμένον Χριστῷ αὐτάρκη καὶ αὐτοδιάκονον καὶ προσέτι ἐφήμερον ἐπαναιρεῖσθαι βίον. οὐ γὰρ ἐν πολέμῳ, ἀλλ᾿ ἐν εἰρήνῃ παιδαγωγούμεθα. πολέμῳ μὲν οὖν πολλῆς δεῖ τῆς παρασκευῆς δαψιλείας τε χρῄζει ἡ τρυφή· εἰρήνη δὲ καὶ ἀγάπη, ἀφελεῖς καὶ ἀπράγμονες ἀδελφαί, οὐχ ὅπλων δέονται, οὐ παρασκευῆς ἀσώτου· λόγος ἐστὶν αὐταῖς ἡ τροφή, ὁ τὴν ἐνδεικτικὴν καὶ παιδευτικὴν ἡγεμονίαν κεκληρωμένος λόγος, παρ᾿ οὗ τὸ εὐτελές τε καὶ ἄτυφον καὶ τὸ ὅλον φιλελεύθερον καὶ φιλάνθρωπον φιλόκαλόν τε ἐκμανθάνομεν, ἑνὶ λόγῳ μετ᾿ οἰκειότητος ἀρετῆς ἐξομοιούμενοι τῷ θεῷ. ἀλλ᾿ ἐκπόνει καὶ μὴ ἀπόκαμνε· ἔσῃ γὰρ οἷος οὐκ ἐλπίζεις οὐδ᾿ εἰκάσαι δύναιο ἄν. ὡς δὲ ἔστι τις ἄλλη μὲν φιλοσόφων ἀγωγή, ἄλλη δὲ ῥητόρων, παλαιστῶν δὲ ἄλλη, οὕτως ἐστὶν γενναία διάθεσις φιλοκάλῳ προαιρέσει κατάλληλος ἐκ τῆς Χριστοῦ παιδαγωγίας περιγινομένη, καὶ τὰ τῆς ἐνεργείας πεπαιδευμέναι σεμναὶ διαπρέπουσιν πορεία καὶ κατάκλισις καὶ τροφὴ καὶ ὕπνος καὶ κοίτη καὶ δίαιτα καὶ ἡ λοιπὴ παιδεία· οὐ γὰρ ὑπέρτονος ἡ τοιάδε ἀγωγὴ τοῦ λόγου, ἀλλ᾿ εὔτονος. ταύτῃ οὖν καὶ σωτὴρ ὁ λόγος κέκληται, ὁ τὰ λογικὰ ταῦτα ἐξευρὼν ἀνθρώποις εἰς εὐαισθησίαν καὶ σωτηρίαν φάρμακα, ἐπιτηρῶν μὲν τὴν εὐκαιρίαν, ἐλέγχων δὲ τὴν βλάβην καὶ τὰς αἰτίας τῶν παθῶν διηγούμενος καὶ τὰς ῥίζας τῶν ἀλόγων ἐκκόπτων ἐπιθυμιῶν, παραγγέλλων μὲν ὧν ἀπέχεσθαι δεῖ, τὰς ἀντιδότους δὲ ἁπάσας τῆς σωτηρίας τοῖς νοσοῦσι προσφέρων· τοῦτο γὰρ τὸ μέγιστον καὶ βασιλικώτατον ἔργον τοῦ θεοῦ, σῴζειν τὴν ἀνθρωπότητα. τῷ μὲν οὖν ἰατρῷ οὐδὲν πρὸς ὑγείαν συμβουλεύοντι ἄχθονται οἱ κάμνοντες, τῷ δὲ παιδαγωγῷ τῷ θείῳ πῶς οὐκ ἂν ὁμολογήσαιμεν τὴν μεγίστην χάριν μὴ σιωπῶντι μηδὲ παρενθυμουμένῳ τὰς εἰς ἀπώλειαν φερούσας ἀπειθείας, ἀλλὰ καὶ ταύτας διελέγχοντι καὶ τὰς ὁρμὰς τὰς εἰς αὐτὰς διατεινούσας ἀνακόπτοντι καὶ τὰς καθηκούσας πρὸς τὴν ὀρθὴν πολιτείαν ὑποθημοσύνας ἐκδιδάσκοντι; πλείστην ἄρα ὁμολογητέον χάριν αὐτῷ. τὸ γάρ τοι ζῷον τὸ λογικόν, τὸν ἄνθρωπον λέγω, ἄλλο τι φαμὲν ἢ θεάσασθαι τὸ θεῖον δεῖν; θεάσασθαι δὲ καὶ τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην φύσιν φημὶ χρῆναι ζῆν τε ὡς ὑφηγεῖται ἡ ἀλήθεια, ἀγαμένους ὑπερφυῶς τόν τε παιδαγωγὸν αὐτὸν καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ὡς πρέποντα ἀλλήλοις ἐστὶ καὶ ἁρμόττοντα· καθ᾿ ἣν εἰκόνα καὶ ἡμᾶς ἁρμοσαμένους χρὴ σφᾶς αὐτοὺς πρὸς τὸν παιδαγωγόν, σύμφωνον τὸν λόγον ποιησαμένους τοῖς ἔργοις, τῷ ὄντι ζῆν.
pass_a_gloss: Having already gone through these things, it would be fitting for us to have Jesus, our pedagogue, outline for us the true life and to educate the person in Christ. The characteristic of Him is not overly frightening, nor is it careless in gentleness. He both commands and characterizes the commandments so that we may be able to carry them out. It seems to me that He Himself formed man from the earth, regenerated him with water, increased him with spirit, educated him with word, guiding him towards sonship and salvation with holy commandments, so that, having transformed the earthly person into a holy and heavenly one from corruption, He may fulfill that divine phrase: 'Let us make man according to the image and likeness of us.' And indeed, Christ became the fulfillment of what God said, while the other man is considered only in the image. We, however, O children of a good Father, nurslings of a good pedagogue, let us fulfill the will of the Father, let us listen to the Word, and truly let us follow the life of our Savior; from here, let us already practice the heavenly citizenship, according to which we are deified, being anointed with the eternal and incorruptible chrism of joy, having the unmistakable example of the Lord's immortality and following the footsteps of God; to whom alone it is fitting to consider and care how the life of men may become healthier. But He also prepares us for self-sufficiency in life and freedom from excess, and for a journey that is easy to travel and straightforward, ready for eternity of well-being, teaching each of us to be the steward of himself. 'Do not worry,' He says, 'about tomorrow,' saying that the life recorded for Christ should be self-sufficient, serving itself, and furthermore, ephemeral, to be rejected. For we are being educated in peace, not in war. War, indeed, requires much preparation and extravagance; but peace and love, unassuming and untroubled sisters, do not need arms, nor do they need reckless preparation; their nourishment is the Word, the Word that has been entrusted with the indicative and educational leadership, from which we learn what is humble and unassuming and philanthropic and loving, being conformed to God with one Word, in familiarity with virtue. But work hard and do not faint; for you will be such as you do not hope for, nor could you imagine. Just as there is one kind of upbringing for philosophers, another for orators, and another for athletes, so there is a noble disposition, suitable for a loving choice, coming from the pedagogy of Christ, and the dignified actions of energy are in harmony with the journey and reclining and nourishment and sleep and bed and diet and the rest of the education; for this kind of upbringing of the Word is not excessive, but moderate. Therefore, the Word is also called Savior, having found the rational medicines for men towards sensitivity and salvation, watching over the opportunity, reproving the harm and explaining the causes of the passions and cutting out the roots of irrational desires, commanding what one should abstain from, and offering all the antidotes of salvation to the sick; for this is the greatest and most royal work of God, to save humanity. The patients do not resent the doctor who advises nothing for their health, so why would we not acknowledge the greatest gratitude to the divine Pedagogue, who does not keep silent or remind us of the disobediences that lead to destruction, but also reproves them and cuts off the impulses that lead to them and teaches the submissions that lead to the right citizenship? We should acknowledge the greatest gratitude to Him. For what else do we say the rational animal, that is, man, needs to do but to contemplate the divine? And to contemplate human nature, I say, one needs to live as truth leads, having taken the Pedagogue Himself and His commandments in a superhuman way, as is fitting and harmonious with each other; according to which image we also, having been harmonized with them, ought to be towards the Pedagogue, having made the Word harmonious with our deeds, to live in reality.

pass_b_english: Having already gone through these matters, it would be fitting for Jesus, our Pedagogue, to outline the true life for us and to educate the person in Christ. His character is not overly frightening, nor is it careless in its gentleness. He both commands and shapes His commandments so that we may be able to carry them out. It seems to me that He Himself formed man from the earth, regenerated him with water, increased him with the Spirit, and educated him with the Word, guiding him toward sonship and salvation by holy commandments, so that, having transformed the earthly person into a holy and heavenly one from corruption, He may fulfill that divine phrase: "Let us make man according to our image and likeness" (Genesis 1:26). And indeed Christ became the full fulfillment of what God said, while the other man is considered only in the image. We, however, O children of a good Father, nurslings of a good Pedagogue, let us fulfill the will of the Father, let us listen to the Word, and truly let us follow the saving life of our Savior; from here let us already practice the heavenly citizenship, according to which we are deified, being anointed with the ever-blooming chrism of joy and the incorruptible chrism of fragrance, having the unmistakable example of the Lord's immortality and following the footsteps of God — to whom alone it belongs to consider and to care how and in what way the life of men might become healthier. But He also prepares us for self-sufficiency in life and freedom from excess, and even for a journey-readiness that is easy to travel and straightforward, for an eternity of well-being, teaching each of us to be the steward of himself. "Do not worry," He says, "about tomorrow," saying that the life enrolled in Christ must be self-sufficient, self-serving, and furthermore ephemeral, to be rejected. For we are being educated not in war, but in peace. War indeed requires much preparation and extravagance; but peace and love, unassuming and untroubled sisters, do not need arms, nor do they need reckless preparation. Their nourishment is the Word, the Word that has been entrusted with the indicative and educational leadership, from which we learn what is humble and unpretentious, and what is wholly freedom-loving and philanthropic and beauty-loving, being conformed to God with one Word in familiarity with virtue. But work hard and do not faint; for you will become such as you do not hope for, nor could you imagine. Just as there is one kind of upbringing for philosophers, another for orators, and another for athletes, so there is a noble disposition, suitable for a beauty-loving choice, coming from the pedagogy of Christ, and the dignified actions of energy distinguish the journey and reclining and nourishment and sleep and bed and diet and the rest of the education; for this kind of upbringing of the Word is not excessive, but moderate. Therefore the Word is also called Savior, having found the rational medicines for men toward sensitivity and salvation, watching over the opportunity, reproving the harm and explaining the causes of the passions and cutting out the roots of irrational desires, commanding what one must abstain from, and offering all the antidotes of salvation to the sick; for this is the greatest and most royal work of God, to save humanity. The patients do not resent the doctor who advises nothing for their health, so why would we not acknowledge the greatest gratitude to the divine Pedagogue, who does not keep silent nor pass over the disobediences that lead to destruction, but also reproves them and cuts off the impulses stretching toward them and teaches the submissions that lead to the right citizenship? We ought to acknowledge the greatest gratitude to Him. For what else do we say the rational animal — that is, man — needs to do but to contemplate the divine? And to contemplate human nature, I say, one needs to live as truth leads, having embraced the Pedagogue Himself and His commandments in a superhuman way, as is fitting and harmonious with each other; according to which image we also, having been harmonized, ought to be toward the Pedagogue, having made the Word harmonious with our deeds, to live in reality.
